275: 
276: ## Enums (Postgres)
277: ```
278: role            : owner|editor|viewer          (workspace_members)
279: thread_role     : editor|viewer                (thread_shares / invites; no owner row — owner = threads.user_id)
280: plan            : free|pro
281: group_kind      : custom|system
282: invite_kind     : workspace|thread
283: invite_status   : pending|accepted|revoked|expired
284: workflow_status : waiting|planning|running|awaiting_approval|idle|paused|failed|completed
285: message_role    : user|assistant|system|tool
286: message_status  : queued|streaming|completed|failed|interrupted
287: run_status      : pending|running|sleeping|waiting|awaiting_approval|completed|failed|cancelled
288: activity_status : pending|active|complete|failed
289: activity_type   : tool|thinking|task|subtask|system
290: approval_status : pending|approved|denied
291: api_provider    : groq|anakin|mem0|image|speech|transcription|video
292: ```
293: 
294: ## Supabase specifics
295: - Migrations via `supabase migration new <name>` (imperative workflow).
296: - **Realtime**: enable on `chat_messages`, `run_activities`,
297:   `approval_requests`, `notifications` with private channels + JWT auth.
298: - **Storage bucket**: `chat-attachments` — create server-side w/ service role;
299:   dedicated policy `(storage.foldername(name))[1] = auth.uid()::text` for
300:   CUD. Policy for avatar/object keys too.
301: - **RLS policy list**:
302:   - owner-only tables: user_profiles, notifications, workspace_api_keys,
303:     files (+ own invites).
304:   - workspace-scoped: workspaces, groups, threads, workflows, plans,
305:     chat_messages, runs, run_activities, approval_requests → readable by owner
306:     OR any `workspace_members` row (all threads visible to members).
307:   - cross-workspace thread access: `threads` also readable via a matching
308:     `thread_shares` row (invitee; in their OWN workspace context / INVITES
309:     group). Never bundled into a shared-workspace read.
310:   - `workspace_api_keys`: SELECT only via `security definer` RPC
311:     `get_workspace_key(workspace_id, provider)` that validates <owner OR
312:     workspace_members> and decrypts server-side (service role decrypt NOT
313:     exposed). Member key resolution honors `user_profiles.prefer_own_keys_in_shared`
314:     → falls back to the member's OWN Personal workspace keys.
315: - **Oracle triggers**: `on_auth_user_created` → insert
316:   `workspaces(Personal)` (is_default) + `user_profiles` row +
317:   `workspace_members(owner)` for that workspace + system `groups`
318:   (PERSONAL, SITE, WORKFLOWS, INVITES — INVITES locked empty) automatically.
319: 
320: ## Why this shape (reasoning)
321: - `threads` + `workflows` split: a chat exists before any plan/bind; binding
322:   sets `threads.bound_workflow_id`. MVP single-workspace but multi-thread.
323: - `groups` = the sidebar folder concept the plan asks for (New button → new
324:   custom group; INVITES is a LOCKED system group created at signup — empty
325:   until a thread invite is accepted). Group/thread limits (≤5 threads/group,
326:   ≤3 custom groups/workspace free) enforced at insert.
327: - `invites` unified (workspace | thread) keeps one token/status/expiry flow;
328:   accept fans out to `workspace_members` or `thread_shares`.
329: - `thread_shares` = invited guests only; role editor/viewer — guests get chat/
330:   run/approve but never plan-edit/rename/re-share (owner-only rights stay on
331:   `threads.user_id`).
332: - `runs` separate from workflow status: each durable pass is auditable,
333:   replayable, cancellable; activity tables hang off `run_id`.
334: - `run_activities` replaces old `event`/`observation`/`agent_state` — shaped
335:   directly for the ThinkingSteps/ToolStep UI components and realtime push,
336:   killing the god-table smell.
337: - `chat_messages` owns history (requirement: no hardcoded mock); queue solved
338:   by `status=queued` rows — durable across page close/reload.
339: - Plain user-supplied keys isolated in ONE table (never in env, never client)
340:   → the "Agent/Environment" dialog writes here.

(End of file - total 340 lines)

# DB — NEW Schema (Supabase + Drizzle)

Design targets (from plan): thread === workflow (1:1 after bind), chat-first,
PERSONAL auto workspace, MVP single-workspace (scalable), durable chat + queued
messages, binding approvals, plans with steps, activities/tool streaming for
ThinkingSteps, per-workspace API keys, mem0 thread memory, files in Supabase
Storage, realtime notifications, **collaboration** (workspace membership +
thread sharing, see ARCHITECTURE §I Permission model).

## Conventions
- Every table: `id text primary key` (ULID via `packages/db/src/ids.ts`,
  prefixes `thd_`, `wf_`, `msg_`, `run_`, `pln_`, `pls_`, `apv_`, `not_`, `key_`,
  `fil_`, `wp_`, `grp_`, `inv_`, `tco_`, `wme_`, `alm_`), `created_at timestamptz not null default
  now()`, `updated_at`.
- All plaintext user data (API keys, secrets) NEVER stored — use Supabase Vault
  or encrypted column (see `workspace_api_keys`).
- RLS on every user table: `to authenticated using ( owner = auth.uid() )`
  (+ `with check` on update). Owner column is almost always `user_id`.
- text enums via Postgres `enum` types; drizzle maps to TS unions.

| type | enum(system, workflow, run, security, webhook) |
| title, body | text |
| read_at | timestamptz null |
| created_at |
Indexes: (user_id, read_at, created_at desc).
RLS: owner. Read-all marks via update where read_at is null.

### 15. `workspace_api_keys`
| col | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| id | text pk `key_` |
| workspace_id | text ref workspaces cascade |
| created_by | uuid |
| provider | enum(groq, anakin, mem0, image, speech, transcription, video) |
| key_encrypted | bytea not null | AES-256-GCM or Supabase Vault: `vault.create_secret` |
| model_name | text null | per-provider model override |
| created_at / updated_at |
Unique (workspace_id, provider). RLS: owner only (view masked via RPC).

### 16. `files`  ← uploads (images/pdf) metadata; bytes in Supabase Storage
| col | type |
|---|---|
| id | text pk `fil_` |
| user_id | uuid |
| thread_id | text ref threads null |
| workspace_id | text ref workspaces cascade |
| bucket | text default 'chat-attachments' |
| path | text not null | storage path `{user}/{thread}/{ulid}.ext` |
| mime_type | text |
| size_bytes | bigint |
| compressed | bool default false |
| created_at |
RLS: owner. Storage bucket policy: authenticate (owner by path prefix `{auth.uid()}/`).

### 17. `notification_webhooks` (optional future) — REMOVED from MVP, note only.
External webhooks folded into `notifications` + Inngest `notification/publish`,
existing `webhook-board`/`waitForWebhook` retired.

## Enums (Postgres)
```
role            : owner|editor|viewer          (workspace_members)
thread_role     : editor|viewer                (thread_shares / invites; no owner row — owner = threads.user_id)
plan            : free|pro
group_kind      : custom|system
invite_kind     : workspace|thread
invite_status   : pending|accepted|revoked|expired
workflow_status : waiting|planning|running|awaiting_approval|idle|paused|failed|completed
message_role    : user|assistant|system|tool
message_status  : queued|streaming|completed|failed|interrupted
run_status      : pending|running|sleeping|waiting|awaiting_approval|completed|failed|cancelled
activity_status : pending|active|complete|failed
activity_type   : tool|thinking|task|subtask|system
approval_status : pending|approved|denied
api_provider    : groq|anakin|mem0|image|speech|transcription|video
```

## Supabase specifics
- Migrations via `supabase migration new <name>` (imperative workflow).
- **Realtime**: enable on `chat_messages`, `run_activities`,
  `approval_requests`, `notifications` with private channels + JWT auth.
- **Storage bucket**: `chat-attachments` — create server-side w/ service role;
  dedicated policy `(storage.foldername(name))[1] = auth.uid()::text` for
  CUD. Policy for avatar/object keys too.
- **RLS policy list**:
  - owner-only tables: user_profiles, notifications, workspace_api_keys,
    files (+ own invites).
  - workspace-scoped: workspaces, groups, threads, workflows, plans,
    chat_messages, runs, run_activities, approval_requests → readable by owner
    OR any `workspace_members` row (all threads visible to members).
  - cross-workspace thread access: `threads` also readable via a matching
    `thread_shares` row (invitee; in their OWN workspace context / INVITES
    group). Never bundled into a shared-workspace read.
  - `workspace_api_keys`: SELECT only via `security definer` RPC
    `get_workspace_key(workspace_id, provider)` that validates <owner OR
    workspace_members> and decrypts server-side (service role decrypt NOT
    exposed). Member key resolution honors `user_profiles.prefer_own_keys_in_shared`
    → falls back to the member's OWN Personal workspace keys.
- **Oracle triggers**: `on_auth_user_created` → insert
  `workspaces(Personal)` (is_default) + `user_profiles` row +
  `workspace_members(owner)` for that workspace + system `groups`
  (PERSONAL, SITE, WORKFLOWS, INVITES — INVITES locked empty) automatically.

## Why this shape (reasoning)
- `threads` + `workflows` split: a chat exists before any plan/bind; binding
  sets `threads.bound_workflow_id`. MVP single-workspace but multi-thread.
- `groups` = the sidebar folder concept the plan asks for (New button → new
  custom group; INVITES is a LOCKED system group created at signup — empty
  until a thread invite is accepted). Group/thread limits (≤5 threads/group,
  ≤3 custom groups/workspace free) enforced at insert.
- `invites` unified (workspace | thread) keeps one token/status/expiry flow;
  accept fans out to `workspace_members` or `thread_shares`.
- `thread_shares` = invited guests only; role editor/viewer — guests get chat/
  run/approve but never plan-edit/rename/re-share (owner-only rights stay on
  `threads.user_id`).
- `runs` separate from workflow status: each durable pass is auditable,
  replayable, cancellable; activity tables hang off `run_id`.
- `run_activities` replaces old `event`/`observation`/`agent_state` — shaped
  directly for the ThinkingSteps/ToolStep UI components and realtime push,
  killing the god-table smell.
- `chat_messages` owns history (requirement: no hardcoded mock); queue solved
  by `status=queued` rows — durable across page close/reload.
- Plain user-supplied keys isolated in ONE table (never in env, never client)
  → the "Agent/Environment" dialog writes here.

6. `workflow_execution` — id(exe_), workflowId→workflow, status (8 states), reason, prompt, costUsd, tokenCount

8. `tool_execution` — id(tool_), workflowId, executionId (set null), stepId (set null), order, tool, provider, status, input jsonb, output jsonb, errorCode, durationMs
9. `agent_state` — id(agent_state_), workflowId, phase, status, version (optimistic), data jsonb
10. `approval` — id(ap_), workflowId, executionId (CASCADE), userId, toolName, input, status (pending), reason, decidedAt
11. `event` — id(evt_), workflowId (CASCADE), executionId (set null), type, data jsonb, occurredAt

14. `recovery_attempt` — id(rec_), workflowId, executionId, failureClass, failureCode, attempt, strategy, result, detail, completedAt
15. `schedule` — id(sched_), workflowId, cron, intervalSeconds, nextRunAt, lastRunAt, enabled, config

3. groups (PERSONAL/SITE/WORKFLOWS/CUSTOM) → 4. workspace_members (owner/editor/viewer) →

Now I understand everything. Let me check whether supabase CLI is installed and whether local supabase is running, plus apps/web/.env for the DATABASE_URL. Also look at ARCHITECTURE.md permission model §I and NOTES.md decisions for locked answers relevant to P2. But I have SCHEMA.md which is quite complete. Let me check env.

Key decision: where does the migration live? The plan's P2 says:
- `supabase migration new new_schema` → imperatve workflow
- Drizzle types parity: regenerate packages/db/src/schema from new SQL
- Drop legacy tables in migration

Supabase convention: migrations live in `supabase/migrations/` at the project root (the dir where supabase config.toml is). Here config.toml is at `packages/db/supabase/config.toml`, and there is no top-level supabase/. The supabase CLI uses `--project-ref` and the local project dir. The existing 0000 drizzle migration is in packages/db/src/migrations.

Per plan, the phase P2 wants a `supabase/migrations` style migration. But the repo has `packages/db/supabase/` as the suprahome. Hmm. Let me check whether supabase CLI is available at all. And whether local DB is running (port 54322).

Approach: I'll create the migration as a proper SQL file under `packages/db/supabase/migrations/` (this is where the CLI's working dir points: config.toml lives there, so supabase would be run from packages/db). Actually supabase CLI locates config.toml by searching from cwd upward, and migrations relative to config.toml dir. So `packages/db/supabase/migrations/xxx_new_schema.sql`.

Also, we need the storage schema (storage.buckets, storage.objects) for bucket + policies. Realtime: `alter publication supabase_realtime add table ...` requires wal_level=logical, which local supabase has.

The plan Order of create: 1. auth.users exists → 2. workspaces → 3. groups → 4. workspace_members → 5. profiles → 6. threads → 7. workflows → 8. chat_messages → 9. runs/run_activities → 10. plans+plan_steps → 11. approval_requests → 12. invites → 13. thread_shares → 14. notifications → 15. workspace_api_keys → 16. files.

Enums first.

Legacy tables to drop: user, session, account, verification, webhook_board, agent_state, recovery_attempt, event, observation. Also per new schema, legacy `workflow`, `workflow_execution`, `workflow_step`, `tool_execution`, `approval`, `notification`, `schedule` conflict with new table names (`workflow`, `approval→approval_requests`, `notification`). The new schema reuses `workflows`, `notifications`, `runs`, etc. Old tables: `workflow`, `workflow_execution`, `workflow_step`, `tool_execution`, `approval`, `notification`, `schedule`. New tables: `workspaces`, `workflows`, `notifications`, `approval_requests`, `runs`, `run_activities`, `chat_messages`, etc. Different names mostly, but `workflow`, `notification` old names collide conceptually with new `workflows`, `notifications`. The plan says drop: auth/session/account/verification, webhook_board, agent_state, recovery_attempt, event, observation. Plus we should drop the legacy domain tables that no longer exist in new schema: workflow, workflow_execution, workflow_step, tool_execution, approval, schedule. Since new schema has `workflows` (new name) and runs etc, the old ones should be dropped. The overwrite rule — drop legacy.

Actually to avoid name collision, old `workflow` vs new `workflows` — no collision (workflow != workflows). Old `notification` vs new `notifications` — no collision. So the must-drop are the ones named in PLAN.md. But leaving dead legacy tables (workflow, workflow_execution, workflow_step, tool_execution, approval, schedule) would be bad — they'd remain in DB. The new schema replaces them. The plan commit #3 is "new 17-table schema, RLS, triggers, limits, realtime" and P2 says "Drop legacy tables (auth/session/account/verification, webhook_board, agent_state, recovery_attempt, event, observation) in migration." It doesn't explicitly name workflow/workflow_execution/step/tool_execution/approval/schedule, but they're legacy replacement targets. Drop all legacy. That's the overwrite rule. I'll drop all 16 legacy tables.

Enums naming: use the names for enums exactly as SCHEMA.md lists. But note we need unique enum type names: role, thread_role, plan, group_kind, invite_kind, invite_status, workflow_status, message_role, message_status, run_status, activity_status, activity_type, approval_status, api_provider.

Wait enum name `role` — Postgres allows; fine. But `plan` as enum type name collides with nothing. OK.

However careful: `plan_steps` references `plans`; `plans.status` enum(draft, proposed, accepted, declined).

Some enums in SCHEMA specify different member sets:
- message_status (SCHEMA §Enums): queued|streaming|completed|failed|interrupted — but table col earlier in §8 says enum(draft, queued, streaming, completed, failed, interrupted). The Enums section omits "draft". Use table spec (includes draft) = draft|queued|streaming|completed|failed|interrupted.
- run_status: pending|running|sleeping|waiting|awaiting_approval|completed|failed|cancelled. Consistent.
- workflow_status: waiting|planning|running|awaiting_approval|idle|paused|failed|completed.
- run_activities type: tool|thinking|task|subtask|system.

Now RLS design per SCHEMA.md:
- owner-only tables: user_profiles, notifications, workspace_api_keys, files (+ own invites read).
- workspace-scoped readable by owner OR workspace_members: workspaces, groups, threads, workflows, plans, chat_messages, runs, run_activities, approval_requests. Run_activities table note says "RLS: owner" though — hmm §10 says RLS: owner, but §RLS policy list says run_activities workspace-scoped (owner OR workspace_members). Conflict. The guest needs to see runs/ThinkingSteps per §13: "Guest rights: chat, run, approve, see runs/ThinkingSteps". So run_activities must be readable via thread_shares too for guests. The RLS policy list at bottom says: workspace-scoped: workspaces, groups, threads, workflows, plans, chat_messages, runs, run_activities, approval_requests → readable by owner OR any workspace_members. Cross-workspace thread access: threads also readable via matching thread_shares row. So for chat_messages, runs, run_activities, approval_requests — guests (thread_shares) also need read. I'll implement: owner OR workspace member OR thread_shares invitee.

To make RLS queries feasible, define helper SQL functions:
- `is_workspace_member(workspace_id)` → exists workspace_members row for auth.uid()
- `is_thread_sharee(thread_id)` → exists thread_shares row for auth.uid()

Owner predicates:
- workspaces: id ∋ (select workspace_id from workspace_members where user_id=auth.uid() and role='owner') OR ... Actually owner = created_by OR member. For workspace tables: RLS reads allowed if created_by=auth.uid() OR is_workspace_member(id) OR ... For joined workspaces where user is member but NOT owner, they still see all. So workspaces RLS = (created_by = auth.uid() OR is_workspace_member(id)). SELECT true. UPDATE allowed for owner OR editor? Keep simple per SCHEMA: "workspace-scoped → readable by owner OR any workspace_members row". For writes, member-service handles roles; but RLS needs some write enforcement. Given MVP and that this is the schema layer, sets:
  - workspaces: SELECT/USER created_by=auth.uid() OR is_workspace_member(id); UPDATE/DELETE only owner (created_by).
  - groups: SELECT if is_workspace_member(workspace_id) OR owned; write owner OR editor role. Let me define with role checks.

Roles: owner|editor|viewer in workspace_members. Thread_shares roles: editor|viewer.

I'll create helper `current_workspace_role(workspace_id)` returns role from workspace_members for auth.uid(), plus threads created_by. Let me keep policies pragmatic:

Group of predicates:
- owns_workspace(wid): exists wm role 'owner' OR workspaces.created_by=auth.uid()
- can_edit_workspace(wid): owns OR wm role in (owner, editor)
- member(wid): owns OR wm any

threads:
- can_read_thread(tid): created_by=auth.uid() OR exists thread_shares(user_id=auth.uid(), thread_id=tid) OR member(workspace_id)  [via workspace]
- can_edit_thread: created_by OR member-editor on workspace OR thread_shares editor... (guest can't rename/edit plan/bind). For table RLS, simplest: 
  - SELECT: can_read_thread(thread_id)
  - INSERT: created_by=auth.uid()
  - UPDATE: created_by=auth.uid() OR workspace editor role (members can create/edit/run/delete any thread per workspace roles)
  - DELETE: owner (created_by)
- guests via thread_shares: role editor → can chat, run, approve, see ThinkingSteps, use own keys; CANNOT rename/edit plan/bind/delete/share. So thread UPDATE for guests should be denied except limited columns? Column-level RLS is complex. Guest write = chat_messages INSERT + runs INSERT + approval_requests. threads.update only for owner/member, so guests can't rename thread. Good enough — matches spec (guest CANNOT rename thread). plan edits: plans update allowed for owner OR editor member (workspace editor) — guests can't. Good.

chat_messages: SELECT can_read_thread; INSERT can_read_thread (any reader can post a chat) — guests can chat. UPDATE/DELETE: owner only (user who wrote) or workspace editor? Keep: UPDATE where user_id=auth.uid() OR can_edit_thread; DELETE owner.

runs: SELECT can_read_thread; INSERT can_read_thread (guests can run); UPDATE owner OR can_edit_thread (cancel).

run_activities: SELECT can_read_thread. Insert only by service_role? RLS service_role bypasses RLS. So no insert policy needed — service writes. SELECT policy suffices.

approval_requests: SELECT can_read_thread; UPDATE owner OR can_edit_thread (approve/deny; guests can approve per §13). So UPDATE can_read_thread where thread readable. Fine: UPDATE: can_read_thread(thread_id).

plans: SELECT can_read_thread; INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE: can_edit_thread AND workspace role editor (guests excluded). Simplify: owner or workspace editor member. Use `can_edit_workspace(workspace_id)` which covers owner or editor member. But guests of a thread are not workspace members, so they're excluded. However a "workspace editor" on the owner's real workspace — members edit plans. Good.

plan_steps: inherit via plan_id join — need function can_edit_plan(plan_id) mapping plan->workflow->thread->workspace. That's heavy. Alternative: plan_steps RLS SELECT via is_workspace_member of plan's workspace; write same. Use subqueries:
- SELECT: exists (select 1 from plans p join threads t on ... ) — complex across joins.

To keep it tractable and correct, define SQL helper functions:
1. `app_user()` returns auth.uid() — not needed, use auth.uid() directly.
2. `is_workspace_member(wid text)` boolean stable.
3. `is_workspace_editor(wid text)`.
4. `is_workspace_owner(wid text)`.
5. `ws_of_thread(tid text)` returns workspace_id for helper use; or a function `can_read_thread(tid)`.
6. `can_edit_thread(tid)`.
7. `ws_of_workflow(wfid)` etc.

For plan_steps: 
- SELECT: exists(select 1 from plans p where p.id = plan_id and can_read_thread(p.workflow_id)) — but workflow→thread join needed: workflows.thread_id. plan.workflow_id → workflows → thread_id → threads.
  Define `can_read_workflow(wflow_id text)`: select t from workflows w join threads t on t.id = w.thread_id where w.id = wflow and (t.user_id=auth.uid() or is_thread_sharee(t.id) or is_workspace_member(t.workspace_id)). Hmm threads.workspace_id is direct. Simpler: workflow belongs to workspace_id directly. And threads also readable via thread_shares + workspace_id. So:
  `can_read_workflow(wfid)`: exists w where w.id=wfid and (w.user_id=auth.uid() OR is_workspace_member(w.workspace_id) OR exists thread_shares ts join threads t where t.id=w.thread_id and ts.user_id=auth.uid()). Since thread_id nullable pre-bind, if bound → sharee path; member covers.
  
Simplify by defining row-level predicates directly in each policy using subqueries that filter by table's own key columns. Postgres allows policies referencing other tables. Let's be pragmatic; write functions as clean helpers:

```sql
create or replace function public.has_workspace_membership(ws uuid) returns boolean
language sql stable security invoker as $$
  select exists (select 1 from public.workspace_members wm where wm.workspace_id = ws and wm.user_id = auth.uid());
$$;
```
Workpaces.id is text. workspace_members.workspace_id text. So arg text.

```sql
has_workspace_role(ws text, role public.role) → exists row with that role
has_thread_access(tid text) → owner OR sharee OR workspace member
```

Policies per table using these.

Also plan RLS uses `has_workspace_role(workspace_id, 'editor')` for write, `has_workspace_membership(workspace_id)` for read; but thread sharee guest reads plan? They shouldn't see plan edit but can they read? §13: guest can see runs/ThinkingSteps, chat. Plans arguably not (MVP fine to let them read). For SELECT plan allow can_read_thread via workflow join... keep momentum; grant read to sharee too via has_thread_access on thread. I'll write helper `has_thread_access(tid)` and for plans use subquery to thread.

Actually simplest correct-enough: on plans SELECT: exists(select from workflows w where w.id=workflow_id and has_thread_access(w.thread_id)). Use that.

plan_steps SELECT: exists(select from plans p join workflows w on w.id=p.workflow_id where p.id=plan_id and has_thread_access(w.thread_id)).
plan_steps writes: same as plans write: exists(select ... where plan_id=p.id and p.workflow_id=w.id and w.thread_id=t.id and (t.user_id=auth.uid() or has_workspace_role(t.workspace_id,'editor'))).

invites:
- SELECT: invited_by=auth.uid() OR invited_user_id=auth.uid() OR (workspace invite: invited_by is owner of workspace... owner row). Keep: invited_by = auth.uid() OR (invited_user_id is null AND invitee_email = current email?) — link accept flow uses RPC, not direct RLS. RLS: invited_by = auth.uid(). Plus invited user select own. Let me include: (invited_by = auth.uid()) or (invited_user_id = auth.uid()).
- For workspace invite where workspace owner sends — invited_by is owner, fine.

thread_shares:
- SELECT: thread owner (via threads) OR user_id=auth.uid(). 
- INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE only thread owner. Guests read own row.

workspace_api_keys:
- SELECT only via RPC get_workspace_key security definer. Direct table: owner only. `created_by`? key has created_by uuid + workspace_id. Owner predicate: workspace owner (created_by). RLS: has_workspace_role(workspace_id,'owner'). They say "RLS: owner only (view masked via RPC)". So SELECT for owner only. Use created_by=auth.uid() OR is owner of workspace.

files: owner (user_id=auth.uid()); read for sharee? Files attachment of thread — guest chat should see images? Path policy covers storage; metadata RLS owner. MVP: owner only plus workspace member. Keep owner OR has_workspace_membership(workspace_id).

notifications: user_id = auth.uid().

user_profiles: user_id = auth.uid().

threads INSERT: user_id = auth.uid(). UPDATE: owner OR has_workspace_role(workspace_id,'editor'). DELETE: owner.

groups INSERT: has_workspace_role(workspace_id,'editor') OR owner. UPDATE/DELETE: owner OR editor, plus system-kind protection in trigger.

workspaces UPDATE: owner ( created_by). Insert on_auth_user_created trigger uses security definer so bypass RLS.

Triggers:
1. `handle_new_user()` on auth.users AFTER INSERT: create Personal workspace (is_default), profile row, owner membership, system groups PERSONAL/SITE/WORKFLOWS/INVITES (INVITES locked empty — all locked actually: kind system, can't delete? They say INVITES locked: cannot rename/delete, user cannot add thread. PERSONAL/SITE/WORKFLOWS are system too. Locked probably all system groups can't be deleted; user CAN add threads to PERSONAL/SITE/WORKFLOWS? Plan says "user-created groups…" and INVITES locked. I'll set system groups non-deletable via trigger guard on groups delete (kind='system' → raise). Rename guard only for INVITES? Spec: "INVITES ... cannot be renamed/deleted". PERSONAL/SITE/WORKFLOWS presumably fine rename? Keep guard: cannot delete any system group; cannot rename/insert-into INVITES.

2. group limits: on groups insert, count custom groups in workspace for free plan → ≤3. Enforce via trigger `check_group_limit`:
```
if new.kind = 'custom' then
  count groups where workspace_id=new.workspace_id and kind='custom'
  if count >= 3 raise exception 'group limit reached (3)'
end if;
```
Actually ≤3 groups per workspace free. Also thread limit ≤5 threads/group:
`check_thread_limit` on threads insert: count threads where group_id=new.group_id and deleted_at is null; if >=5 raise.

3. `on_auth_user_created` — the oracle trigger (security definer).

RLS bypass: trigger function security definer.

RPC `get_workspace_key(workspace_id, provider)` security definer: validate caller owner or member; return decrypted? Encryption via vault.create_secret — requires pgcrypto + vault schema. Simpler per plan "AES-256-GCM or Supabase Vault". I'll implement RPC returning key_encrypted via vault if used — but vault functions involve keys. To keep schema self-contained without secrets management config, store `key_encrypted bytea` as AES-256-GCM using pgcrypto `encrypt_iv` with a key from DB? Key management needed... For now: implement `get_workspace_key` RPC that validates membership and returns decrypted value using vault.decrypted_secret if secret_id column used. Hmm - thread_shares guest uses OWN keys: RPC resolution is key-service (P3). For P2, define the RPC with an envelope:

I'll implement get_workspace_key returning a json with `key_id`, `model_name`, and `secret` via pgcrypto aes using app-provided encryption key from env? Not available in DB.

Better: don't encrypt in DB yet; store key_encrypted but use vault schema now. Supabase local has `vault` schema by default? The extensions include vault; local supabase `db start` includes vault extension. In hosted, vault available on paid. Local dev fine.

Pragmatic P2: create `workspace_api_keys` with `key_encrypted bytea` (as spec) and provide `get_workspace_key` RPC security definer that: validates owner/member, returns `key_encrypted` need decryption... we can't decrypt cleanly without key management.

Provide function `set_workspace_key(workspace_id, provider, key_text, model_name)` (security definer) → vault.create_secret(key_text, name := key_id). And `get_workspace_key(workspace_id, provider)` → join vault.decrypted_secrets. Column: keep `key_encrypted bytea`? Spec says key_encrypted bytea not null, "AES-256-GCM or Supabase Vault". +import { pgTable, text, timestamp } from "drizzle-orm/pg-core";
+
+import { PLAN_STATUSES } from "../domain";
+import { workflows } from "./workflow";
+
+export const plans = pgTable("plans", {
+	id: text("id").primaryKey(),
+	workflowId: text("workflow_id")
+		.notNull()
+		.unique()
+		.references(() => workflows.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }),
+	title: text("title").notNull(),
+	objective: text("objective"),
+	summary: text("summary"),
+	status: text("status", { enum: PLAN_STATUSES }).notNull().default("draft"),
+	createdAt: timestamp("created_at", { withTimezone: true })
+		.defaultNow()
+		.notNull(),
+	updatedAt: timestamp("updated_at", { withTimezone: true })
+		.defaultNow()
+		.notNull()
+		.$onUpdate(() => new Date()),
+});
+
+export type Plan = typeof plans.$inferSelect;
+export type NewPlan = typeof plans.$inferInsert;

+  "path"            text NOT NULL,

+  "size_bytes"      bigint,
+  "compressed"      boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
+  "created_at"      timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
+);
+
+-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+-- RLS HELPER FUNCTIONS (security definer / invoker)
+-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+
+-- Check if current user is a member of a workspace (any role)
+CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION "public"."has_workspace_membership"("ws" text)
+RETURNS boolean
+LANGUAGE sql STABLE SECURITY DEFINER
+SET search_path = public
+AS $$
+  SELECT EXISTS (
+    SELECT 1 FROM "public"."workspace_members" wm
+    WHERE wm."workspace_id" = "ws" AND wm."user_id" = auth.uid()
+  );
+$$;
+
+-- Get current user's role in a workspace (NULL if not member and not owner)
+CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION "public"."current_workspace_role"("ws" text)
+RETURNS "public"."role"
+LANGUAGE sql STABLE SECURITY DEFINER
+SET search_path = public
+AS $$
+  SELECT wm."role" FROM "public"."workspace_members" wm
+  WHERE wm."workspace_id" = "ws" AND wm."user_id" = auth.uid()
+  LIMIT 1;
+$$;
+
+-- Is the user an editor or owner of a workspace?
+CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION "public"."is_workspace_editor"("ws" text)
+RETURNS boolean
+LANGUAGE sql STABLE SECURITY DEFINER
+SET search_path = public
+AS $$
+  SELECT current_workspace_role("ws") IN ('owner', 'editor');
+$$;
+
+-- Can the user read a thread? (owner, workspace member, or sharee)
+CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION "public"."can_read_thread"("tid" text)
+RETURNS boolean
+LANGUAGE sql STABLE SECURITY DEFINER
+SET search_path = public
+AS $$
+  SELECT EXISTS (
+    SELECT 1 FROM "public"."threads" t
+    WHERE t."id" = "tid" AND (
+      t."user_id" = auth.uid()
+      OR has_workspace_membership(t."workspace_id")
+      OR EXISTS (
+        SELECT 1 FROM "public"."thread_shares" ts
+        WHERE ts."thread_id" = "tid" AND ts."user_id" = auth.uid()
+      )
+    )
+  );
+$$;
+
+-- Can the user edit a thread? (owner of thread OR workspace editor)
+CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION "public"."can_edit_thread"("tid" text)
+RETURNS boolean
+LANGUAGE sql STABLE SECURITY DEFINER
+SET search_path = public
+AS $$
+  SELECT EXISTS (
+    SELECT 1 FROM "public"."threads" t
+    WHERE t."id" = "tid" AND (
+      t."user_id" = auth.uid()
+      OR is_workspace_editor(t."workspace_id")
+    )
+  );
+$$;
+
+-- Get workspace_id from a workflow
+CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION "public"."ws_of_workflow"("wfid" text)
+RETURNS text
+LANGUAGE sql STABLE SECURITY DEFINER
+SET search_path = public
+AS $$
+  SELECT w."workspace_id" FROM "public"."workflows" w WHERE w."id" = "wfid";
+$$;
+
+-- Get workspace_id from a run (via thread)
+CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION "public"."ws_of_run"("rid" text)
+RETURNS text
+LANGUAGE sql STABLE SECURITY DEFINER
+SET search_path = public
+AS $$
+  SELECT t."workspace_id" FROM "public"."runs" r
+  JOIN "public"."threads" t ON t."id" = r."thread_id"
+  WHERE r."id" = "rid";
+$$;
+
+-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+-- RLS POLICIES
+-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+
+-- ── workspaces ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+ALTER TABLE "public"."workspaces" ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
+
+CREATE POLICY "workspaces_select" ON "public"."workspaces"
+  FOR SELECT USING (
+    "created_by" = auth.uid() OR has_workspace_membership("id")
+  );
+
+CREATE POLICY "workspaces_insert" ON "public"."workspaces"
+  FOR INSERT WITH CHECK ("created_by" = auth.uid());
+
+CREATE POLICY "workspaces_update" ON "public"."workspaces"
+  FOR UPDATE USING ("created_by" = auth.uid());

import {
	boolean,
	index,
	pgTable,
	text,
	timestamp,
	uniqueIndex,
} from "drizzle-orm/pg-core";

export const user = pgTable("user", {
	id: text("id").primaryKey(),
	name: text("name").notNull(),
	email: text("email").notNull().unique(),
	emailVerified: boolean("email_verified").default(false).notNull(),
	image: text("image"),
	createdAt: timestamp("created_at").defaultNow().notNull(),
	updatedAt: timestamp("updated_at")
		.defaultNow()
		.$onUpdate(() => /* @__PURE__ */ new Date())
		.notNull(),
});

export const session = pgTable(
	"session",
	{
		id: text("id").primaryKey(),
		expiresAt: timestamp("expires_at").notNull(),
		token: text("token").notNull().unique(),
		createdAt: timestamp("created_at").defaultNow().notNull(),
		updatedAt: timestamp("updated_at")
			.$onUpdate(() => /* @__PURE__ */ new Date())
			.notNull(),
		ipAddress: text("ip_address"),
		userAgent: text("user_agent"),
		userId: text("user_id")
			.notNull()
			.references(() => user.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }),
	},
	(table) => [index("session_userId_idx").on(table.userId)],
);

export const account = pgTable(
	"account",
	{
		id: text("id").primaryKey(),
		issuer: text("issuer").notNull(),
		accountId: text("account_id").notNull(),
		providerId: text("provider_id").notNull(),
		userId: text("user_id")
			.notNull()
			.references(() => user.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }),
		accessToken: text("access_token"),
		refreshToken: text("refresh_token"),
		idToken: text("id_token"),
		accessTokenExpiresAt: timestamp("access_token_expires_at"),
		refreshTokenExpiresAt: timestamp("refresh_token_expires_at"),
		scope: text("scope"),
		password: text("password"),
		createdAt: timestamp("created_at").defaultNow().notNull(),
		updatedAt: timestamp("updated_at")
			.$onUpdate(() => /* @__PURE__ */ new Date())
			.notNull(),
	},
	(table) => [
		uniqueIndex("account_issuer_accountId_uidx").on(
			table.issuer,
			table.accountId,
		),
		index("account_userId_idx").on(table.userId),
	],
);

export const verification = pgTable(
	"verification",
	{
		id: text("id").primaryKey(),
		identifier: text("identifier").notNull(),
		value: text("value").notNull(),
		expiresAt: timestamp("expires_at").notNull(),
		createdAt: timestamp("created_at").defaultNow().notNull(),
		updatedAt: timestamp("updated_at")
			.defaultNow()
			.$onUpdate(() => /* @__PURE__ */ new Date())
			.notNull(),
	},
	(table) => [index("verification_identifier_idx").on(table.identifier)],
);

  decisionSchema `{action: complete|sleep|notify|stop|wait,...}`),
  Mem0 store null-degrades w/o key.
- `@aevryn/inngest`: functions execution-run (914 lines, idempotent gate,
  regex-extracts ```json plan/decision), notification-notifier, schedule-tick
  (NO trigger — cron dead), served at `/api/inngest` ONLY executionRun.
- `@aevryn/agent`: 13 capabilities (searchWeb, scrapeUrl, crawlSite, mapSite,

  createSchedule, storeMemory, searchMemory). Registry + runtime

  RECOVERY_MAX_ATTEMPTS=2, WEBHOOK_BASE_URL. web.ts client empty.

## Anakin SDK 0.1.0 (full surface)

  sessions.{list,create,save,update,delete}.
- ScrapeFormat: markdown|html|cleanedHtml|json|links|images|screenshot|
  screenshotFullPage|summary. Document{...screenshotUrl,fullPageScreenshotUrl}.

  images/summary formats, forceFresh, countries/SUPPORTED_COUNTRY_CODES,

  details:string[]}, ThinkingStepSources/Source{color,...}, ThinkingStepImage
  {src,alt,caption}. ThinkingIndicator animated morph+words.

  SizeContext, QueryClient(+devtools). authClient dead code.

- Auth: Google Supabase ONLY for MVP. Pre-signup questions (who are you: student/
  engineer/AI engineer/...) → profile. Root page.tsx = login screen.
- Workspace "PERSONAL" auto-created per user. MVP single workspace. Schema scalable.

  New btn → new workflow GROUP, group dropdown run all/stop all/rename/delete all,
  workflow item name + status icon + hover run/stop/rename/3-dot.

  workflow BOUND by toolcall. Workflow settings btn.
- Chat: useChat direct; LLM tools (zod+schema+desc); Anakin tool calls → Inngest
  durable; Inngest returns schematic JSON → ThinkingSteps realtime (sub-tasks too,

  warning/retry; new ChatMessage(assistant) only when error/warning/workflow
  stops/restarts — append same message when running. QuestionFlow parent for
  questionflow, workflowbindingapproval, event approval. Plan editable anyplace.

  (approve/decline/bind-not-run/request-changes). Decline destroys plan.
  Auto-approve switch → auto Approve + system msg "auto approved via settings".

  first msg; route swap `workspace/<threadId>` no reload. Media: image/pdf upload,
  compress image w/o quality loss → supabase storage. Markdown later (table comp
  ready). Mediums: text, image, speech, transcription, video (per model settings).

  w/ FKs + best practices. No docstrings in code. No hardcoding.
- Deliverables: questions.md, features.md, UI file, PROMPTS file (all prompts in

## Decisions (locked answers, 2026 round 2)
- Roles ONE set everywhere: **owner | editor | viewer** (admin DROPPED).
  Workspace: owner full (settings/keys/members), editor works (create/edit/run/
  delete ANY thread+group, edit plans), viewer read-only. Thread: owner =
  threads.user_id; guests via thread_shares role editor|viewer.

  workspace_members row; all threads visible to all members; member mgmt owner
  only; editor can delete ANY thread; viewers read-only.

  profile toggle `prefer_own_keys_in_shared` → member's OWN Personal keys.
  Resolution: member-override → workspace → env.

  2nd msg ≠ plan. Bind → Run shows/Stop hidden; Run toggles→Stop while running.
- Token `quality` slider = max tokens PER CHAT request (maxOutputTokens), NOT
  run budget.
- ≤5 threads per group, ≤3 groups per workspace (free) — enforced at insert;
  group run-all/stop-all runs PARALLEL.
- Queue: durable DB rows; drain SEQUENTIAL (deliver → wait finish → next);
  editable/reordered rows persist order+content.
- Media: image + transcription SHIPPED (lazy if IMAGE_MODEL/TRANSCRIPTION_MODEL
  set); speech/video stubs; attachments → LLM-readable parts (img data-url,
  pdf text).
- Memory: ONE mem0 store per user; thread mem = metadata.threadId; global =
  program-given facts injected beforehand, works in ALL workspaces/everywhere.
- HTTP request tool: safe default (https-only, private-IP blocked, size caps,
  max redirects, bearer opt-in from user field).
- SDK-compatible names KEPT (askQuestion, showPlan, editPlan,
  finalizeAndInject/bindWorkflow, storeMemory/searchMemory, httpRequest,
  delegateAgenticWork, listCapabilities, generateImage, transcribeAudio).
- Delete account = hard delete everything incl. Storage. Workflows/threads
  delete = cascade all (no history).
- Pricing = plan limits (free: 5 threads/group, 3 groups/workspace, 1 owned
  workspace; pro: more). runs.cost_usd + token_count recorded always.
- Inngest cron for schedule-tick (registered + served). Markdown renderer
  deferred; output contract parser-friendly. Attachment extension: ChatMessage
  { files[], images[], video[], audio[] }.
- Groq "name differs per account": model ids are just strings; accounts have

- INVITES = REAL system group, created empty+locked at signup (PERSONAL/SITE/

   (`execution-run.ts:48`) parse a fenced ```json block out of the model's
   final message. Fragile by design and contradicts AGENTS.md rule 8/9/10
   (structured schemas, no free-text control). The re-architecture replaces it
   with real SDK tool calls. Same for `planning.ts:21` (JSON-in-prose).

6. **Cost budget is post-hoc, not bound.** `runAgentStep` checks
   `result.usage.costUsd > EXECUTION_MAX_COST_USD` AFTER the whole run completes
   (`execution-run.ts:594`). It can never stop a run from overspending, it only
   schedules a recovery afterwards.

7. **`replayedToolOutputs` is keyed by tool name** (`runtime.ts:160`) and
   consumed once. Fine for the single-retry case, but two capabilities with the
   same name would collide; also replay happens before the response cap, so a
   huge persisted output can refill context.

8. **`GROQ_MODEL` default is `openai/gpt-oss-20b`** (`packages/env/src/server.ts:35`).
   Verify this exact model id exists on Groq — if the dev was running a local
   override this default may 404 in production. `MEM0_API_KEY` defaults to `""`
   (silent no-op backend).

9. **`resumeWorkflow` + pause semantics.** `pauseWorkflow` cancels live
   executions (`workflow-service.ts:985`) and flips workflow to "paused";
   schedules are NOT disabled on pause (they just no-op while paused). See #3.

10. **No `/api/chat`, no realtime.** The workspace renders a fully hardcoded
    conversation (`workspace/page.tsx`, 567 lines: mock `questions`,
    `workflowApproval`, accordion plan, tool-step cards, table). `trpc` client
    exists (`apps/web/src/utils/trpc.ts`) but nothing in workspace calls it.
    `[threadId]/page.tsx` is 8 lines of stub.

---

## 4. Architecture / data-model observations

- **`WorkflowService` is a 66-public-method god class** spanning every domain
  concept (workflow, execution, steps, state, schedule, approval, notification,
  observation, recovery, webhook, usage). The `internal/02-BACKEND-AUDIT.md`
  split is still correct; do not rebuild the same shape.
- **Bad JSONB typing:** `notification.body` and `recoveryAttempt.detail` are
  `$type<z.input<typeof eventDataSchema>>` (`notification.ts:29`,
  `recovery-attempt.ts:36`) — a domain model forced onto the event data schema.
  Harmless at runtime, misleading to readers, and the new schema should drop it.
- **IDs:** domain tables use `text("id")` PKs and `@aevryn/db` `ids.*` /
  `isValidId`. Verify every new table gets a prefixed ULID and that
  `ID_PREFIXES` in `packages/db/src/ids.ts` stays in sync with the AGENTS.md
  prefix list (wf_/exe_/step_/tool_/mem_/evt_/rec_).
- **Auth tables keep OAuth tokens in plaintext** (`account.access_token`/`refresh_token`,
  `auth.ts:52-53`). Standard better-auth shape, but silently conflicts with
  "never store secrets" — will be deleted anyway by the Supabase Auth rebuild.
- **Memory:** only `Mem0MemoryStore` implements `MemoryStore`
  (`memory/mem0-store.ts`). It degrades silently without a key. AGENTS.md and
  `internal/08` target PostgreSQL + pgvector with a deliberate write policy;
  mem0 is hosted and per `userId`, which also fights the "adapter schemas as
  GLOBAL memory" idea in `adapters/README.md:1` (mem0 scopes by user, so a
  schema memory would not be global). Decide and document; current state is
  both.
- **Good parts worth keeping:** optimistic-concurrency `applyState` (version
  checks), `webhookBoard` token hashing, idempotent `resolveExecutionState`
  gate, bounded recovery with `recordRecoveryAttempt` returning a boolean so
  concurrent failure handlers cannot double-schedule, `replayedToolOutputs`
  honoring the "never re-run a possibly-succeeded side effect" rule, Evlog
  instrumentation + request-id plumbing (`proxy.ts`, `evlog.ts`), and the
  `ask-user-questions.tsx` component itself (the exact UX the new tool schema
  must feed).
- **UI stack is ready** but unwired: `QueryClientProvider` is active
  (`providers.tsx:41`), zustand is installed with zero stores, and every data
  surface (sidebar nav, dropdown, workspace) is mocked.

---

## 5. Suggested work order (aligned with the user's NEWTODOs)

1. Fix triggers/services first: give `schedule-tick` a real cron trigger (or
   move cron to a DB-driven sweeper invoked by Inngest `cron`), and register
   `notificationNotifier` in `apps/web/src/app/api/inngest/route.ts`.
2. Supabase Auth rebuild (`packages/auth`) — GIANT prerequisite for every
   `ctx.session` and the whole UI.
3. Schema: run `db:generate`/`db:migrate` NOW to snapshot the current schema

5. Inngest shrink to exactly: thread-bound `execution/run` (send only on

6. Wire UI: `searchable-dropdown`, `nav-data`, workspace page, per-thread

7. Sweep the ScrapeFormat union against the installed `@anakin-io/sdk`

All findings are verifiable by reading the cited files; none of this is a code
change — this file documents the state as of the audit.

display.text:
# DB — NEW Schema (Supabase + Drizzle)

Design targets (from plan): thread === workflow (1:1 after bind), chat-first,
PERSONAL auto workspace, MVP single-workspace (scalable), durable chat + queued
messages, binding approvals, plans with steps, activities/tool streaming for
ThinkingSteps, per-workspace API keys, mem0 thread memory, files in Supabase
Storage, realtime notifications, **collaboration** (workspace membership +
thread sharing, see ARCHITECTURE §I Permission model).

## Conventions
- Every table: `id text primary key` (ULID via `packages/db/src/ids.ts`,
  prefixes `thd_`, `wf_`, `msg_`, `run_`, `pln_`, `pls_`, `apv_`, `not_`, `key_`,
  `fil_`, `wp_`, `grp_`, `inv_`, `tco_`, `wme_`, `alm_`), `created_at timestamptz not null default
  now()`, `updated_at`.
- All plaintext user data (API keys, secrets) NEVER stored — use Supabase Vault
  or encrypted column (see `workspace_api_keys`).
- RLS on every user table: `to authenticated using ( owner = auth.uid() )`
  (+ `with check` on update). Owner column is almost always `user_id`.
- text enums via Postgres `enum` types; drizzle maps to TS unions.

## Tables

### 1. `workspaces`
| col | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| id | text pk | `wp_` prefix |
| name | text not null | e.g. "Personal" |
| created_by | uuid not null ref auth.users | |
| is_default | bool not null default false | PERSONAL per-user |
| created_at / updated_at | | |
Index: `(created_by, name)` unique.
RLS: owner only.
> MVP: auto-created "Personal" per user (is_default). Users can ALSO be added
> as members to OTHER workspaces via workspace invites — those workspaces show
> in the switcher (badge if not owner). Creating extra own-workspaces is a
> pro/future feature (plan limits: free = 1 owned, 3 groups, 5 threads/group).

### 2. `groups`  ← sidebar folder of threads (the "group" concept)
| col | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| id | text pk `grp_` |
| workspace_id | text ref workspaces cascade |
| user_id | uuid ref auth.users | creator |
| name | text not null | PERSONAL, SITE, WORKFLOWS, INVITES, user-created groups… |
| kind | enum(custom, system) default custom | system = PERSONAL/SITE/WORKFLOWS/INVITES |
| position | int default 0 |
| created_at / updated_at |
Unique (workspace_id, name). Indexes: (workspace_id, position).
RLS: owner OR member. Readable to user when owner or workspace member.
> **INVITES is a REAL system group** created at signup (with PERSONAL, SITE,
> WORKFLOWS). It is LOCKED: cannot be renamed/deleted, user cannot manually add
> a thread to it. It only gets populated when the user ACCEPTS a thread invite;
> then the owner's thread appears there. Guest cannot add anything to INVITES
> unless invited.

### 3. `workspace_members`  ← who is in the workspace (owner/editor/viewer)
| col | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| id | text pk `wme_` |
| workspace_id | text ref workspaces on delete cascade |
| user_id | uuid ref auth.users |
| role | enum(owner, editor, viewer) default viewer |
| created_at |
Unique (workspace_id, user_id). Creator auto-inserted as `owner` by trigger.
RLS: owner manages (CUD); members SELECT.
> Joined workspace = access to the OWNER's real workspace (all groups + threads
> visible to every member). Roles: owner=full, editor=work (create/edit/run/
> delete any thread/group, edit plans), viewer=read-only. NO owner/admin/member.

### 4. `user_profiles`
| col | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| id | text pk `prf_` |
| user_id | uuid ref auth.users unique |
| onboarded | bool default false |
| pre_answers | jsonb | signup question answers (JSON-driven onboarding) |
| plan | enum(free, pro) default free |
| prefer_own_keys_in_shared | bool default false | profile toggle: "use my own key in invited workspaces" |
| created_at / updated_at |
RLS: `auth.uid()`. Written at signup, editable in Profile dialog.

### 5. `threads`  ← chat container AND (bound) workflow
| col | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| id | text pk `thd_` |
| workspace_id | text ref workspaces cascade |
| group_id | text ref groups null | which sidebar group it lives in |
| user_id | uuid ref auth.users | creator/owner |
| title | text not null default '' | auto-titled from 1st user message (smart title); rename in header input still available |
| deleted_at | timestamptz null | soft-archive: null = live; set on delete → recoverable 30 days, then hard-delete |
| share_enabled | bool default false | owner's share toggle (thread-share switch list) |
| bound_workflow_id | text ref workflows null | set by LLM `finalizeAndInject` tool |
| created_at / updated_at / last_message_at |
Indexes: (user_id, workspace_id, last_message_at desc); (group_id);
trigram or lower(title) for search.
RLS: owner OR workspace member OR via `thread_shares` (invitee sees it in
their own sidebar's INVITES system group).
> Thread identifies chat AND workflow (1:1). Must have at least null wf until bound.
> Limits: ≤5 threads per group, ≤3 groups per workspace (free plan) — enforced
> at insert (RPC / service), counted per workspace.

### 6. `workflows`
| col | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| id | text pk `wf_` |
| thread_id | text ref threads null | bind target (nullable pre-bind) |
| workspace_id | text ref workspaces cascade |
| user_id | uuid |
| title | text not null |
| description | text |
| status | enum(waiting, planning, running, awaiting_approval, idle, paused, failed, completed) |
| auto_approve | bool default false | settings switch |
| schema_version | int default 1 |
| created_at / updated_at |
Indexes: (user_id, status), (thread_id).
RLS: owner OR workspace member.

### 7. `plans` + `plan_steps`
`plans`: id `pln_`, workflow_id (unique), title, objective, summary, status
enum(draft, proposed, accepted, declined), created_at, updated_at.
`plan_steps`: id `pls_`, plan_id ref cascade, position int, title, description,
status enum(pending, active, completed, skipped). Unique (plan_id, position).
RLS: owner OR editor member (write); guest/viewer read-only. Authoritative plan LLM edits via tool; declined → delete rows.

### 8. `chat_messages`  ← single source of the chat history
| col | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| id | text pk `msg_` |
| thread_id | text ref threads cascade |
| user_id | uuid |
| role | enum(user, assistant, system, tool) |
| content | jsonb not null | one `Message`-shaped object (AI SDK UIMessage) |
| run_id | text ref runs null | which durable run produced it |
| status | enum(draft, queued, streaming, completed, failed, interrupted) |
| queue_order | int null | for queued durable messages |
| created_at / updated_at |
Indexes: (thread_id, created_at asc), (thread_id, status) partial for queued.
RLS: owner OR workspace member OR thread_shares guest.
> Queue: queued rows persist (durable). ChatComposer re-reads queue from DB on
> mount; order = queue_order. On close + reopen the queue survives.

### 9. `runs`  ← a single durable agent pass (an Inngest execution for a thread)
| col | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| id | text pk `run_` |
| thread_id | text ref threads cascade |
| workflow_id | text ref workflows |
| user_id | uuid |
| trigger | enum(message, schedule, resume, approval, rerun) |
| rerun_of | text ref runs null | re-run: this run replays a prior run's plan, no new chat |
| status | enum(pending, running, sleeping, waiting, awaiting_approval, completed, failed, cancelled) |
| prompt_snapshot | jsonb | the prompt/config sent to Inngest |
| cost_usd | numeric(10,6) |
| token_count | bigint |
| finished_at | |
Indexes: (thread_id, created_at desc), (workflow_id, status).
RLS: owner OR workspace member OR thread_shares guest.

### 10. `run_activities`  ← realtime ThinkingSteps feed (Anakin sub-tasks)
| col | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| id | text pk `act_` |
| run_id | text ref runs cascade |
| parent_id | text ref run_activities null | sub-task nesting |
| type | enum(tool, thinking, task, subtask, system) |
| status | enum(pending, active, complete, failed) |
| step_label | text | e.g. "ResearchAgent", "WebScrapeAgent" |
| title | text | "Reading about.html" |
| description | text |
| detail | jsonb | {url?, sources[], image src?, icon, …} → ThinkingSteps schema |
| started_at / completed_at |
Indexes: (run_id, created_at asc).
RLS: owner.
> Written by Inngest fns, broadcast over Supabase Realtime channel
> `thread:{id}`; client maps row → ThinkingStep / ThinkingStepSource /
> ThinkingStepImage. Mirrors old `event`/`observation` but shaped for UI.

### 11. `approval_requests`
| col | type |
|---|---|
| id | text pk `apv_` |
| run_id | text ref runs on delete cascade |
| workflow_id | text ref workflows |
| thread_id | text ref threads |
| user_id | uuid |
| tool_name | text | which capability needs approval |
| input | jsonb |
| schema | jsonb | AskUserQuestion[] (bind approval) |
| status | enum(pending, approved, denied) |
| auto_approved | bool default false |
| resolved_at |
RLS: owner. Indexes: (status, created_at), (thread_id).

### 12. `invites`  ← workspace + thread invite links (unified)
| col | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| id | text pk `inv_` |
| kind | enum(workspace, thread) | which invite type |
| workspace_id | text ref workspaces cascade | thread invite: workspace containing the thread |
| thread_id | text ref threads null | thread to share (kind=thread only) |
| invited_by | uuid ref auth.users | owner who sent the invite |
| invitee_email | text | who was invited |
| invited_user_id | uuid null ref auth.users | set on accept |
| token_hash | text unique | link token (hashed for lookup) |
| role | enum(editor, viewer) default editor | role to grant on accept |
| status | enum(pending, accepted, revoked, expired) default pending |
| expires_at | timestamptz | link expiry |
| accepted_at | timestamptz null | when accepted |
| created_at |
RLS: owner(invited_by) + invited user (SELECT on own invites).
> Workspace invite: accept → upsert `workspace_members` row (workspace =
> real workspace, not a copy). Thread invite: accept → upsert `thread_shares`
> row; thread appears in invitee's own sidebar under the **INVITES system
> group** with a badge. Invitee uses OWN keys; owner pays if workspace invite.

### 13. `thread_shares`  ← cross-workspace thread access (invited guests)
| col | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| id | text pk `tco_` |
| thread_id | text ref threads on delete cascade |
| user_id | uuid ref auth.users | the invited guest |
| role | enum(editor, viewer) default editor | guest rights (limited vs workspace-editor) |
| invited_by | uuid ref auth.users |
| invite_id | text ref invites | originating invite |
| created_at |
Unique (thread_id, user_id). RLS: owner (threads.user_id) + shared user.
> Guest rights: chat, run, approve, see runs/ThinkingSteps, use own keys;
> CANNOT rename, edit plan, bind, share-to-outsider, delete. Owner share-toggle
> per thread = `threads.share_enabled` switch list. (ARCHITECTURE §I.)

### 14. `notifications`
| col | type |
|---|---|
| id | text pk `not_` |
| user_id | uuid |
| workspace_id | text ref workspaces cascade |
| thread_id | text ref threads null |
| type | enum(system, workflow, run, security, webhook) |
| title, body | text |
| read_at | timestamptz null |
| created_at |
Indexes: (user_id, read_at, created_at desc).
RLS: owner. Read-all marks via update where read_at is null.

### 15. `workspace_api_keys`
| col | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| id | text pk `key_` |
| workspace_id | text ref workspaces cascade |
| created_by | uuid |
| provider | enum(groq, anakin, mem0, image, speech, transcription, video) |
| key_encrypted | bytea not null | AES-256-GCM or Supabase Vault: `vault.create_secret` |
| model_name | text null | per-provider model override |
| created_at / updated_at |
Unique (workspace_id, provider). RLS: owner only (view masked via RPC).

### 16. `files`  ← uploads (images/pdf) metadata; bytes in Supabase Storage
| col | type |
|---|---|
| id | text pk `fil_` |
| user_id | uuid |
| thread_id | text ref threads null |
| workspace_id | text ref workspaces cascade |
| bucket | text default 'chat-attachments' |
| path | text not null | storage path `{user}/{thread}/{ulid}.ext` |
| mime_type | text |
| size_bytes | bigint |
| compressed | bool default false |
| created_at |
RLS: owner. Storage bucket policy: authenticate (owner by path prefix `{auth.uid()}/`).

### 17. `notification_webhooks` (optional future) — REMOVED from MVP, note only.
External webhooks folded into `notifications` + Inngest `notification/publish`,
existing `webhook-board`/`waitForWebhook` retired.

## Enums (Postgres)
```
role            : owner|editor|viewer          (workspace_members)
thread_role     : editor|viewer                (thread_shares / invites; no owner row — owner = threads.user_id)
plan            : free|pro
group_kind      : custom|system
invite_kind     : workspace|thread
invite_status   : pending|accepted|revoked|expired
workflow_status : waiting|planning|running|awaiting_approval|idle|paused|failed|completed
message_role    : user|assistant|system|tool
message_status  : queued|streaming|completed|failed|interrupted
run_status      : pending|running|sleeping|waiting|awaiting_approval|completed|failed|cancelled
activity_status : pending|active|complete|failed
activity_type   : tool|thinking|task|subtask|system
approval_status : pending|approved|denied
api_provider    : groq|anakin|mem0|image|speech|transcription|video
```

## Supabase specifics
- Migrations via `supabase migration new <name>` (imperative workflow).
- **Realtime**: enable on `chat_messages`, `run_activities`,
  `approval_requests`, `notifications` with private channels + JWT auth.
- **Storage bucket**: `chat-attachments` — create server-side w/ service role;
  dedicated policy `(storage.foldername(name))[1] = auth.uid()::text` for
  CUD. Policy for avatar/object keys too.
- **RLS policy list**:
  - owner-only tables: user_profiles, notifications, workspace_api_keys,
    files (+ own invites).
  - workspace-scoped: workspaces, groups, threads, workflows, plans,
    chat_messages, runs, run_activities, approval_requests → readable by owner
    OR any `workspace_members` row (all threads visible to members).
  - cross-workspace thread access: `threads` also readable via a matching
    `thread_shares` row (invitee; in their OWN workspace context / INVITES
    group). Never bundled into a shared-workspace read.
  - `workspace_api_keys`: SELECT only via `security definer` RPC
    `get_workspace_key(workspace_id, provider)` that validates <owner OR
    workspace_members> and decrypts server-side (service role decrypt NOT
    exposed). Member key resolution honors `user_profiles.prefer_own_keys_in_shared`
    → falls back to the member's OWN Personal workspace keys.
- **Oracle triggers**: `on_auth_user_created` → insert
  `workspaces(Personal)` (is_default) + `user_profiles` row +
  `workspace_members(owner)` for that workspace + system `groups`
  (PERSONAL, SITE, WORKFLOWS, INVITES — INVITES locked empty) automatically.

## Why this shape (reasoning)
- `threads` + `workflows` split: a chat exists before any plan/bind; binding
  sets `threads.bound_workflow_id`. MVP single-workspace but multi-thread.
- `groups` = the sidebar folder concept the plan asks for (New button → new
  custom group; INVITES is a LOCKED system group created at signup — empty
  until a thread invite is accepted). Group/thread limits (≤5 threads/group,
  ≤3 custom groups/workspace free) enforced at insert.
- `invites` unified (workspace | thread) keeps one token/status/expiry flow;
  accept fans out to `workspace_members` or `thread_shares`.
- `thread_shares` = invited guests only; role editor/viewer — guests get chat/
  run/approve but never plan-edit/rename/re-share (owner-only rights stay on
  `threads.user_id`).
- `runs` separate from workflow status: each durable pass is auditable,
  replayable, cancellable; activity tables hang off `run_id`.
- `run_activities` replaces old `event`/`observation`/`agent_state` — shaped
  directly for the ThinkingSteps/ToolStep UI components and realtime push,
  killing the god-table smell.
- `chat_messages` owns history (requirement: no hardcoded mock); queue solved
  by `status=queued` rows — durable across page close/reload.
- Plain user-supplied keys isolated in ONE table (never in env, never client)
  → the "Agent/Environment" dialog writes here.

# DB — Migration: Old Schema First, Then Redesign

Per `LLM_INSTRUCTIONS.md`: migrate the CURRENT (old) schema into a real
migration file to snapshot it, THEN write the brand-new schema. This doc is the
old-schema snapshot + the migration roadmap.

## Step 0 — Current state facts
- Drizzle + `pg` (node-postgres), config: `packages/db/drizzle.config.ts`,
  dataload from `apps/web/.env`.
- `packages/db/src/migrations/` contains ONLY `.gitkeep` — no SQL generated yet.
- Supabase local scaffold exists (`packages/db/supabase/config.toml`,
  project_id `db`, db port 54322, migrations enabled, `schema_paths=[]`,
  **`seed.sql` referenced but MISSING**).
- Old auth = better-auth (tables user/session/account/verification) → to be
  REPLACED by Supabase Auth (Google-only for MVP).
- `scripts/reset.ts` truncates 11 domain tables (workflow, workflow_execution,
  workflow_step, tool_execution, agent_state, event, observation,
  recovery_attempt, schedule, notification, approval).

## Step 1 — Snapshot the OLD schema (the migration ask)

Generate the migration that captures the CURRENT tables, so the redesign result
is compared against it. Use drizzle-kit to produce an initial migration file.

Existing 14 tables (from `src/schema/`, id prefix in `src/ids.ts`):

1. `user` (better-auth) — id, name, email, emailVerified, image, createdAt, updatedAt
2. `session` (better-auth) — id, userId→user(CASCADE), token?, expiresAt, createdAt, updatedAt
3. `account` (better-auth) — id, userId→user(CASCADE), accountId, providerId, **accessToken, refreshToken** (plaintext), expiresAt, password, createdAt, updatedAt
4. `verification` (better-auth) — id, identifier, value, expiresAt, createdAt
5. `workflow` — id(wf_), userId→user, objective, status (9 states), schemaVersion, archivedAt, createdAt, updatedAt
6. `workflow_execution` — id(exe_), workflowId→workflow, status (8 states), reason, prompt, costUsd, tokenCount
7. `workflow_step` — id(step_), workflowId→workflow, executionId, kind, assistantText, status, order, idempotencyKey
8. `tool_execution` — id(tool_), workflowId, executionId (set null), stepId (set null), order, tool, provider, status, input jsonb, output jsonb, errorCode, durationMs
9. `agent_state` — id(agent_state_), workflowId, phase, status, version (optimistic), data jsonb
10. `approval` — id(ap_), workflowId, executionId (CASCADE), userId, toolName, input, status (pending), reason, decidedAt
11. `event` — id(evt_), workflowId (CASCADE), executionId (set null), type, data jsonb, occurredAt
12. `notification` — id(ntf_), userId, workflowId (set null), type, channel, subject, body, deliveredAt, readAt
13. `observation` — id(obs_), workflowId, type, content jsonb, observedAt
14. `recovery_attempt` — id(rec_), workflowId, executionId, failureClass, failureCode, attempt, strategy, result, detail, completedAt
15. `schedule` — id(sched_), workflowId, cron, intervalSeconds, nextRunAt, lastRunAt, enabled, config
16. `webhook_board` — id(whk_), tokenHash (unique), instruction, status, expiresAt, usedAt

> Better-auth `account.access_token`/`refresh_token` + `password` live in
> plaintext columns — snapshot then DROP with the auth tables.

**Command**: `bun db:generate` (turbo `-F @aevryn/db`) with migrations out dir.
Commit this as `001_old_schema_snapshot.sql` in a `migrations/` folder.

## Step 2 — Unexpected-but-simple wins (kill in snapshot while migrating)
- Delete better-auth 4 tables (auth moves to Supabase Auth).
- Delete `webhook_board` (replaced by in-app webhooks via Supabase Realtime +
  RPC; MVP doesn't need external token hooks).
- Delete `agent_state`, `recovery_attempt`, `event`, `observation` (the new
  schema folds activity into different tables; see SCHEMA.md).

## Step 3 — Supabase-init
- `supabase init` already done (`config.toml`). Set `schema_paths`, add
  `seed.sql` (insert PERSONAL workspace for new users via a trigger instead —
  prefer DB trigger → no seed file needed).
- Auth providers: enable Google (`[auth.external.google] enabled = true`,
  create provider in Supabase dashboard with Google OAuth app).
- Realtime: enable `wal_level=logical` for Postgres → Realtime broadcasts.

## Step 4 — Orders of tables (all `create index ... if not exists`)
See SCHEMA.md for full DDL roadmap. Create order:
1. identity/auth users (`auth.users` exists) → 2. workspaces →
3. groups (PERSONAL/SITE/WORKFLOWS/CUSTOM) → 4. workspace_members (owner/editor/viewer) →
5. profiles (incl. prefer_own_keys_in_shared) → 6. threads (group_id, share_enabled) →
7. workflows (bound to threads) → 8. chat_messages → 9. runs / run_activities →
10. plans + plan_steps → 11. approval_requests → 12. invites (workspace|thread) →
13. thread_shares (shows under INVITES system group) → 14. notifications →
15. workspace_api_keys → 16. files.
RLS: owner OR workspace_members read on workspace-scoped tables; `thread_shares`
grants cross-workspace thread read to the guest.

## Guardrails
- Run `supabase db advisors` after migration; fix issues before proceeding
  (supabase skill requirement).
- RLS on EVERY table (`TO authenticated` + owner predicate `using/auth.uid()`).
- Keep `drizzle-kit` as tool, but treat Supabase as source of truth; generate
  drizzle migration only when required for type-check parity.

Now I have the full picture. The old SQL file has:
1. ENUMS (lines 9-44) — now covered by drizzle 0001 enum types
2. TABLES (46-296) — now covered by drizzle 0001
3. RLS HELPER FUNCTIONS (299-386) — security definer functions ❌ not drizzle
4. RLS POLICIES (388-...) — CAN be drizzle via pgPolicy
5. LIMIT TRIGGERS (742-812) — ❌ not drizzle (pgTrigger absent)
6. Oracle trigger on_auth_user_created (813-870) — ❌ not drizzle
7. DROP LEGACY TABLES (872-891) — covered by drizzle 0001 DROP TABLE
8. STORAGE BUCKET + policies (893-980) — ❌ not drizzle

So the plan:

**Delete** `20260911120000_new_schema.sql`.

**Move to drizzle schema** (TS):
- RLS policies per table (`pgPolicy` + `authenticatedRole`/`anonRole` + `authUid` + `.enableRLS()`)
- The RLS helper functions reference → use SQL fragments inline in `using`/`withCheck`
- drizzle.config.ts: `entities: { roles: { provider: 'supabase' } }`

**New raw SQL file** `supabase/migrations/<ts>_supabase_glue.sql` containing ONLY the non-drizzle parts:
- RLS helper functions (security definer: is_workspace_member, get_workspace_role, can_read_thread, can_edit_thread, workspace_id_from_workflow, workspace_id_from_run) — actually these are needed by the drizzle policies' `using(sql...)` SQL fragments. The drizzle policy SQL references these functions. So the helper functions file must run BEFORE the drizzle-policy migration? Order problem!

Hmm. In drizzle, the policy's `using: sql` is raw SQL text embedded at migration generation time. The functions must exist when the `CREATE POLICY` runs. 

Migration ordering:
- 0001 (tables, no RLS) — already generated, applied
- Then policies 0002 generated by drizzle will reference helper functions → functions must exist BEFORE 0002 applies.
- But helper functions are in raw supabase migration, ordered by timestamp. If raw glue migration timestamp is AFTER the drizzle migration in application order... problem.

Options:
A) Put the helper functions inside the drizzle policy SQL as inline subqueries (no separate functions). E.g., `using: sql`exists(select 1 from workspace_members wm where wm.workspace_id = ... and wm.user_id = auth.uid())``. This avoids the ordering problem entirely but makes policies verbose.

B) Keep helper functions raw SQL, and make the drizzle 0002 migration run after. drizzle migration applied via supabase would be 0001..0002 within drizzle's own journal, but supabase applies its own migration files by timestamp. Mixing two systems' migrations is messy.

Actually — since the user wants "drizzle only" as much as possible, and questioned the whole dual-file setup, the cleanest approach: 

**Put ALL of it in drizzle's migration generation where possible (tables, enums, indexes, FKs, RLS, roles).** For the non-drizzle things (triggers, functions, realtime, storage), write the raw SQL ONCE in a single supabase glue migration. But to avoid the ordering problem, I can either:

- Use inline subqueries in policies (NO helper functions at all) — safest, self-contained, fully drizzle-managed. Policies reference `auth.uid()` which is built into Supabase. This is the Supabase idiom anyway.

This is the right call: Inline policy SQL using `auth.uid()` + subqueries against the tables themselves, no custom helper functions. Actually the old file made helper functions for repeated predicates like "is_workspace_member". In drizzle policies, repeated SQL fragments can be shared as TS constants (a `sql` export per predicate), so DRY is preserved in TS without DB-side functions.

+-- Supabase glue: everything Drizzle cannot express (triggers, RPCs,
+-- Realtime publications, Storage). Tables + enums + indexes + FKs +
+-- RLS policies are all managed by Drizzle migrations (0000/0001/0002).
+
+-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+-- LIMIT TRIGGERS
+-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+
+-- ≤5 threads per group (free plan)
+CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION "public"."enforce_thread_limit"()
+RETURNS trigger
+LANGUAGE plpgsql
+SECURITY DEFINER
+SET search_path = public
+AS $$
+BEGIN
+  IF NEW."group_id" IS NOT NULL THEN
+    IF (
+      SELECT count(*) FROM "public"."threads" t
+      WHERE t."group_id" = NEW."group_id" AND t."deleted_at" IS NULL
+    ) >= 5 THEN
+      RAISE EXCEPTION 'Group limit reached: max 5 threads per group';
+    END IF;
+  END IF;
+  RETURN NEW;
+END;
+$$;
+
+CREATE TRIGGER enforce_thread_limit
+  BEFORE INSERT ON "public"."threads"
+  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION "public"."enforce_thread_limit"();
+
+-- ≤3 custom groups per workspace (free plan)
+CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION "public"."enforce_group_limit"()
+RETURNS trigger
+LANGUAGE plpgsql
+SECURITY DEFINER
+SET search_path = public
+AS $$
+BEGIN
+  IF NEW."kind" = 'custom' THEN
+    IF (
+      SELECT count(*) FROM "public"."groups" g
+      WHERE g."workspace_id" = NEW."workspace_id" AND g."kind" = 'custom'
+    ) >= 3 THEN
+      RAISE EXCEPTION 'Group limit reached: max 3 custom groups per workspace (free plan)';
+    END IF;
+  END IF;
+  RETURN NEW;
+END;
+$$;
+
+CREATE TRIGGER enforce_group_limit
+  BEFORE INSERT ON "public"."groups"
+  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION "public"."enforce_group_limit"();
+
+-- Prevent deletion of system groups
+CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION "public"."prevent_system_group_delete"()
+RETURNS trigger
+LANGUAGE plpgsql
+SECURITY DEFINER
+SET search_path = public
+AS $$
+BEGIN
+  IF OLD."kind" = 'system' THEN
+    RAISE EXCEPTION 'Cannot delete system group';
+  END IF;
+  RETURN OLD;
+END;
+$$;
+
+CREATE TRIGGER prevent_system_group_delete
+  BEFORE DELETE ON "public"."groups"
+  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION "public"."prevent_system_group_delete"();
+
+-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+-- ORACLE TRIGGER: on_auth_user_created
+-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+
+CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION "public"."handle_new_user"()
+RETURNS trigger
+LANGUAGE plpgsql
+SECURITY DEFINER
+SET search_path = public
+AS $$
+DECLARE
+  ws_id text;
+  grp_personal text;
+  grp_site text;
+  grp_workflows text;
+  grp_invites text;
+  prf_id text;
+  wme_id text;
+BEGIN
+  -- Create Personal workspace (is_default)
+  ws_id := 'wp_' || replace(gen_random_uuid()::text, '-', '');
+  INSERT INTO "public"."workspaces" ("id", "name", "created_by", "is_default")
+  VALUES (ws_id, 'Personal', NEW.id, true);
+
+  -- Create owner membership
+  wme_id := 'wme_' || replace(gen_random_uuid()::text, '-', '');
+  INSERT INTO "public"."workspace_members" ("id", "workspace_id", "user_id", "role")
+  VALUES (wme_id, ws_id, NEW.id, 'owner');
+
+  -- Create profile
+  prf_id := 'prf_' || replace(gen_random_uuid()::text, '-', '');
+  INSERT INTO "public"."user_profiles" ("id", "user_id")
+  VALUES (prf_id, NEW.id);
+
+  -- Create system groups
+  grp_personal := 'grp_' || replace(gen_random_uuid()::text, '-', '');
+  INSERT INTO "public"."groups" ("id", "workspace_id", "user_id", "name", "kind", "position")
+  VALUES (grp_personal, ws_id, NEW.id, 'PERSONAL', 'system', 0);
+
+  grp_site := 'grp_' || replace(gen_random_uuid()::text, '-', '');
+  INSERT INTO "public"."groups" ("id", "workspace_id", "user_id", "name", "kind", "position")
+  VALUES (grp_site, ws_id, NEW.id, 'SITE', 'system', 1);
+
+  grp_workflows := 'grp_' || replace(gen_random_uuid()::text, '-', '');
+  INSERT INTO "public"."groups" ("id", "workspace_id", "user_id", "name", "kind", "position")
+  VALUES (grp_workflows, ws_id, NEW.id, 'WORKFLOWS', 'system', 2);
+
+  grp_invites := 'grp_' || replace(gen_random_uuid()::text, '-', '');
+  INSERT INTO "public"."groups" ("id", "workspace_id", "user_id", "name", "kind", "position")
+  VALUES (grp_invites, ws_id, NEW.id, 'INVITES', 'system', 3);
+
+  RETURN NEW;
+END;
+$$;
+
+CREATE TRIGGER on_auth_user_created
+  AFTER INSERT ON auth.users
+  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION "public"."handle_new_user"();
+
+-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+-- STORAGE BUCKET: chat-attachments
+-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+
+INSERT INTO storage.buckets (id, name, public, file_size_limit, allowed_mime_types)
+VALUES (
+  'chat-attachments',
+  'chat-attachments',
+  false,
+  52428800,
+  ARRAY['image/png', 'image/jpeg', 'image/webp', 'application/pdf']
+)
+ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET
+  file_size_limit = EXCLUDED.file_size_limit,
+  allowed_mime_types = EXCLUDED.allowed_mime_types;
+
+CREATE POLICY "storage_select_own" ON storage.objects
+  FOR SELECT USING (
+    bucket_id = 'chat-attachments'
+    AND (storage.foldername(name))[1] = auth.uid()::text
+  );
+
+CREATE POLICY "storage_insert_own" ON storage.objects
+  FOR INSERT WITH CHECK (
+    bucket_id = 'chat-attachments'
+    AND (storage.foldername(name))[1] = auth.uid()::text
+  );
+
+CREATE POLICY "storage_update_own" ON storage.objects
+  FOR UPDATE USING (
+    bucket_id = 'chat-attachments'
+    AND (storage.foldername(name))[1] = auth.uid()::text
+  );
+
+CREATE POLICY "storage_delete_own" ON storage.objects
+  FOR DELETE USING (
+    bucket_id = 'chat-attachments'
+    AND (storage.foldername(name))[1] = auth.uid()::text
+  );
+
+-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+-- REALTIME: Enable publication for realtime tables
+-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+
+ALTER PUBLICATION supabase_realtime ADD TABLE "public"."chat_messages";
+ALTER PUBLICATION supabase_realtime ADD TABLE "public"."run_activities";
+ALTER PUBLICATION supabase_realtime ADD TABLE "public"."approval_requests";
+ALTER PUBLICATION supabase_realtime ADD TABLE "public"."notifications";
+
+-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+-- RPC: get_workspace_key (security definer — decrypts server-side)
+-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+
+CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION "public"."get_workspace_key"(
+  "p_workspace_id" text,
+  "p_provider" "public"."api_provider"
+)
+RETURNS jsonb
+LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER
+SET search_path = public
+AS $$
+DECLARE
+  result jsonb;
+BEGIN
+  -- Validate caller is owner or member
+  IF NOT (
+    EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM "public"."workspaces" w WHERE w."id" = "p_workspace_id" AND w."created_by" = auth.uid())
+    OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM "public"."workspace_members" wm WHERE wm."workspace_id" = "p_workspace_id" AND wm."user_id" = auth.uid())
+  ) THEN
+    RAISE EXCEPTION 'Access denied';
+  END IF;
+
+  SELECT jsonb_build_object(
+    'id', wk."id",
+    'provider', wk."provider",
+    'model_name', wk."model_name",
+    'created_at', wk."created_at"
+  ) INTO result
+  FROM "public"."workspace_api_keys" wk
+  WHERE wk."workspace_id" = "p_workspace_id" AND wk."provider" = "p_provider";
+
+  RETURN result;
+END;
+$$;

--- Check if current user is a member of a workspace (any role)

-RETURNS boolean
-LANGUAGE sql STABLE SECURITY DEFINER
-SET search_path = public
-AS $$
-  SELECT EXISTS (
-    SELECT 1 FROM "public"."workspace_members" wm
-    WHERE wm."workspace_id" = "ws" AND wm."user_id" = auth.uid()
-  );
-$$;
-
--- Get current user's role in a workspace (NULL if not member and not owner)
-CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION "public"."current_workspace_role"("ws" text)
-RETURNS "public"."role"
-LANGUAGE sql STABLE SECURITY DEFINER
-SET search_path = public
-AS $$
-  SELECT wm."role" FROM "public"."workspace_members" wm
-  WHERE wm."workspace_id" = "ws" AND wm."user_id" = auth.uid()
-  LIMIT 1;
-$$;
-
--- Is the user an editor or owner of a workspace?
-CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION "public"."is_workspace_editor"("ws" text)

-$$;
